course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Graphs
unit.blurb: Linear functions and their tables, plotting straight-line graphs, gradient and y-intercept, and interpreting real-life graphs.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand that a linear function y = mx + c gives a straight line, and complete tables of values.

O2.t: Plot graphs of linear functions, including those written implicitly (e.g. 2x + 3y = 12).

O3.t: Find the gradient and y-intercept of a straight line from its equation or two points, and recognise parallel lines.

O4.t: Interpret real-life graphs, including distance–time and conversion graphs, and find rates of change.

p: An equation like **y = 3x − 2** is a **linear function**: every x gives one y, and the points lie on a **straight line**.
Make a **table of values**: choose x values, substitute, and find y.

lesson.t: Is the point on the line?

p: Linear functions have **x to the power 1 only**: y = 4x + 1, y = 7 − x, y = x/2. Functions such as y = x² or y = 1/x are **not** linear – their graphs are curves.

p: In **y = mx + c**, **m is the gradient** (steepness) and **c is the y-intercept** (where the line crosses the y-axis).
Gradient from two points: **m = (change in y) ÷ (change in x)** = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Lines going down to the right have a negative gradient. **Parallel lines have the same gradient.**

p: On a **distance–time graph** the gradient is the **speed**. A horizontal section means the object has **stopped**. Steeper means faster.
On a **conversion graph** (e.g. dollars to euros) read across and down. The gradient is the **rate** (e.g. euros per dollar).
